extraFacts.fact: 316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 stainless steel; 316 contains molybdenum, which improves resistance to chlorides and pitting, so it is chosen for sea water, coastal plant and chloride-bearing process fluids.

extraFacts.fact: Stainless steel threads can gall (seize and tear) when made up dry, so threads on stainless fittings are lubricated before assembly.

DIN 2353 / ISO 8434-1 24° cone fittings seal with a cutting ring that bites into the tube when the nut is tightened; the tube is cut square and deburred and the ring is pre-assembled before final tightening.
For 10 mm tube the DIN 2353 thread is M14×1.0 in the extra-light (LL) series, M16×1.5 in the light (L) series and M18×1.5 in the heavy (S) series; the series are not interchangeable.

faqs.q: What does the DIN 2353 × NPT Male Connector, Light Series connect to?

faqs.q: How do I install the DIN 2353 × NPT Male Connector, Light Series without leaks or galling?
faqs.a: To fit the Stainless Steel DIN 2353 × NPT Male Connector, Light Series: cut the tube square, deburr it and pre-assemble the nut and cutting ring so the ring bites into the tube before final tightening. Stainless threads can gall if made up dry, so lubricate them. See our [stainless DIN 2353 guide](/blog/stainless-din-2353-and-flareless-bite-fittings).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the light and heavy series DIN 2353 × NPT Male Connector?

For 10 mm tube the thread is M14×1.0 in the extra-light series, M16×1.5 in the light series and M18×1.5 in the heavy series. This listing has 14 part numbers, 6 mm to 42 mm tube.
